title: Cache shadow & headroom tactical — weekly notes
content:
Context: Quick tactical sync capturing the shadow-cache experiments and the headroom/eviction heuristics we've been iterating on. This is a working doc from the Aug 24 weekly sync — purpose is to centralize short-term actions, observed perf numbers, and follow-ups for kernel and batching owners. Informal notes — expect fragments + TODOs.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Shadow cache (write-only shadow copy of KV) is behaving stably under steady-state traffic; gives ~12–18% token-cost reduction for conversational prefix reuse in synthetic workload A, but introduces a 2–5ms p95 penalty on short requests when coalescing is enabled.
- Kernel branch patch-kv-shadow-opt-5.3 reduced lock contention in prefill path; CPU steal dropped from 32% -> 18% on worker nodes during high-throughput tests.
- Headroom heuristic (adaptive token budget per GPU) needs further tuning; observed oscillation when autoscaler and headroom both react to the same burst.

Benchmarks snapshot (synthetic A: 80% chat, avg seq 128 prefill, 32 generation):
- baseline (no shadow): 16.8k tokens/s, p95 latency 42ms
- shadow-enabled, conservative evict: 19.4k tokens/s, p95 latency 44–46ms
- shadow-enabled + patch-kv-shadow-opt-5.3: 20.1k tokens/s, p95 latency 43ms
- shadow + aggressive batch-coalesce: 22.0k tokens/s, p95 latency (short reqs) 47–52ms (regression for <64-token requests)
Notes: raw numbers in linked benchmark CSV. Throughput gains mostly from reduced redundant prefill work; latency impact appears correlated with coalescer scheduling delay.

Today’s meeting notes (Aug 24 — 09:30 standup):
- Marcus: kernel patch discussion. Patch 5.3 landed in feature branch, needs one more perf run on hw-prod-3. Notable change: replaced one global prefill_rw lock with per-shard fine-grain mutex + per-request writer hints. Action: Marcus to run run-crit-3 (long-run 2h) and upload profiles (INF-4872).
- Aisha: shadow cache metrics. Saw higher miss amplification for new-user sessions (cold prefixes) — suspect that shadow write rate is higher than eviction window leading to increased memory churn. Action: add per-session TTL heuristics to shadow logger; Aisha to prototype TTL=5min and compare. Deadline: Aug 31.
- Liam: batching coalescer. Found that when headroom is low, coalescer batches too aggressively and holds short requests waiting to hit batch_size, causing short-request regressions. Proposed change: decouple coalescer patience from headroom controller; introduce small 'latency-priority' mode for requests <64 tokens. Action: Liam to open RFC + bench (INF-4923).
- Evelyn: autoscaler interplay. Autoscaler scales up on p95 crossing SLO, but headroom controller increases per-GPU budget at the same time — combined effect overshoots capacity and then scales down, causing oscillation. Action: add jitter/dampening to headroom changes and make autoscaler consider pending scale decisions. Evelyn to test a dampening window of 45s.

Action items (owner — short-term):
- Marcus Li: run run-crit-3 with patch-kv-shadow-opt-5.3 on hw-prod-3, collect flamegraphs, push to PR comments. (Due Aug 26)
- Aisha Romero: prototype per-session shadow TTL=5min; run cold-start workload; share metric dashboard and delta. (Due Aug 31)
- Liam O'Connor: RFC for coalescer-latency-priority and bench results; ensure <64-token requests target single-request latency SLO. (Due Sep 2)
- Evelyn Zhang: implement dampening/jitter in headroom controller and run 30m stability test under bursty traffic. (Due Aug 28)
- Priya: coordinate canary rollout plan for shadow cache on dedicated pool (10% traffic), prepare rollback checklist. (Due Aug 29)

Open questions / risks:
- Memory accounting in shadow path: right now shadow entries are charged to the same LRU pool; if we keep shadow writes longer, we risk evicting hot KV entries. We should consider a separate soft quota for shadow. (Related: design doc on Confluence)
- Does shadow cache violate any isolation assumptions for Private deployments? Need security sign-off; tag S&C.
- Measurement noise: p95 delta for short requests looks small but consistently present — is it scheduling delay or kernel path overhead? Marcus suspects scheduling; Liam suspects coalescer hold. Plan: isolate by running shadow with coalescer off and vice versa.

Retro / what worked:
- Per-shard mutex approach immediately reduced observed contention in CPU profiles — good win for kernel team.
- Synthetic workload uncovered short-request regressions fast — keep the augmented workload in perf harness.

Notes-to-self (scratchpad):
- Try alternate eviction key: prefer dropping longest-stale shadow entries first (not just LRU).
- Metric to add: shadow_write_vs_hit_ratio per session, plus eviction-induced-prefill_count.
- Add /metrics/kv/shadow_memory_total gauge to Prom.

References and links (quick):
- INF-4872: kernel patch performance run items
- INF-4923: coalescer latency RFC (draft)
- PR 3421: initial shadow-cache implementation (draft)
- Slack: #runtime-kv-cache long thread Aug 22-24 — see pinned messages for logs
- Bench artifact: gs://redwood-perf/kv-shadow/aug24/raw-results.csv

Appendix — quick debug checklist for oncall (short):
- If p95 short requests spike after deploy:
  1) check coalescer patience metric (coalescer.patience_ms)
  2) if patience > 20ms and requests <64 tokens, flip latency-priority flag
  3) check prefill queue depth and kernel lock wait histograms
  4) if kernel lock wait > 5ms p95, roll back patch-kv-shadow-opt-5.3 and trigger Marcus run (INF-4872)

End of notes — this doc will be iterated; feel free to copy fragments into PR descriptions / sprint tasks.
